edits.new:
This bidang usaha is closed to a PT PMA on both annexes of Perpres 49/2021: Lampiran II (p.3, item 11 "Industri batik", sub-rows "Industri batik tulis" and "Industri batik kombinasi tulis dan cap", ex-KBLI 2020 13134) allocates hand-drawn and combined batik to Koperasi and UMKM, and Lampiran III entry #2 ("Industri batik cap") reserves stamped batik to domestic capital. The steps below are the Koperasi/UMKM or domestic-company registration route, not a PMA one.
1. **NIB via OSS** — register on oss.go.id as a Koperasi/UMKM or wholly domestic-owned entity, select this code, issued automatically (1–3 days)
2. **NIB + Standard Certificate** (Small, Medium-Low risk) — Authority: Bupati/Walikota — automatic
3. **NIB + Standard Certificate** (Medium, Medium-High risk) — Authority: Bupati/Walikota — 7 Hari
4. **Submit industrial data report every 6 months (Kemenperin)** — post-license obligation
5. **Pencantuman spesifikasi, komposisi bahan dan/atau care label pada produk atau kemasan yang membuktık...** — post-license obligation
6. **Memiliki dokumen hasil kalıbrası peralatan quality control secara periodık atau hasil uji laboratori...** — post-license obligation

**Authority by scale:**
Small: **Bupati/Walikota** (Otomatis) · Medium: **Bupati/Walikota** (7 Hari)

**PMA:** Closed to foreign investment — domestic entities only. Perpres 10/2021 Lampiran II (as replaced by 49/2021) allocates batik tulis and batik kombinasi to Koperasi and UMKM, and Lampiran III requires domestic capital for batik cap; together they cover every method 13133 names, so a PT PMA cannot hold equity in this activity.

edits.new: Starting a premium batik tulis or cap production facility to supply Bali's booming resort wear and fashion industry? 13133 is reserved to Koperasi, UMKM and domestic capital under Perpres 49/2021 Lampiran II and III, so it is not a PT PMA code — here is what the record says.

edits.old: Bali has a thriving market for premium resort wear incorporating authentic batik textiles. As a foreign investor establishing a PT PMA, you need IDR 2.5 billion paid-up capital. Total investment must still exceed IDR 10 billion per 5-digit KBLI per location — a separate threshold from the paid-up minimum (Permen BKPM 5/2025 art. 26(2) and art. 26(10)). Environmental compliance is the biggest hurdle here; the dyeing process produces liquid waste, so your facility must have a verified wastewater management system (IPAL). Failing to manage dye runoff will result in an immediate shutdown by local Banjars or environmental agencies.
edits.new: Bali has a thriving market for premium resort wear incorporating authentic batik textiles, but the producer cannot be a PT PMA: Perpres 49/2021 Lampiran II allocates batik tulis and batik kombinasi to Koperasi and UMKM and Lampiran III reserves batik cap to domestic capital, so 13133 is closed to foreign ownership anywhere in Indonesia — a foreign brand sources finished batik from an Indonesian producer instead. For the domestic producer, environmental compliance is the biggest hurdle here; the dyeing process produces liquid waste, so the facility must have a verified wastewater management system (IPAL). Failing to manage dye runoff will result in an immediate shutdown by local Banjars or environmental agencies.
